text:
Hi Winnie!

Thank you for your patience! I blocked some time tomorrow to prepare this
for you, and plan to have it over *by EOD tomorrow*.

Additionally, our Security team had a few specific questions regarding
potentially *integrating Encord into our Zero Trust Environment*.
Quoting our InfoSec team:

To clarify our zero-trust priorities, we’re exploring network access
controls, specifically evaluating whether platform access can be restricted
to traffic from our ZScaler IP ranges. We understand multi-tenant SaaS
platforms have architectural constraints around tenant-specific IP
restrictions. We’d like to explore:

   1. Native IP allowlisting capabilities at the tenant level (if available)
   2. Integration options with our existing SSO and ZScaler infrastructure
   3. Enterprise customers’ common approach to this type of use case.

subject: RE: Compliance & Pricing
text:
Thank you for your rapid response, Alex as always.

Licensing

Answering your questions, and remembering I am looking at R&D Sandbox version for our internal experiments:

  *   How many labellers/geologists would need access to the platform for internal use?

License say up to 3 geologists as this is just a sandbox.

  *   How many images do you envisage bringing into the platform?

50,000 images in the next few months, mostly test sets of core data.  Also, we wish to experiment with point cloud labelling.
For our production premise servers, we are doing hundreds of thousands of core images per customer (there are 1 billion core images in the sector), and labelling teams will scale up based on attributes and consistency of style of input.   Largely what we are validating in the test bed are the labelling resources required and compute by doing smaller experiments on different diverse data sets.
For now, please focus on an initial price for a R&D test bed for us, which I believe will have a low consumption rate of data and minimal labellers to begin. The idea is to later have the miner purchase their own vision hub and we curate their models in their own on-premises versions so it is very important we understand how you charge your fees.
Compliance
Thank you for sharing the Compliance Assessment Report for comment.  If you could send me the feedback and evidence from your governance team particularly around ISO27001.  Do you currently have any mining companies placing their data in your cloud?  Why has several of your opposition reached this standard if SOC II suffices (for example Labelbox)?
I will reach out on our side to get clarification under our supplier status with BHP and others around ISO 27001 requirements, just want to ensure we don’t have roadblocks to commercialisation later.
Best regards,
[image]
Richard Sojka    EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR

subject: Re: Encord & Tau
text:
Hi Jamie,

Thanks for the chat today. Here is a google drive folder with to example
videos from our robots:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XjzlD2sN-yhthykqmL5mO41UP1fE0fdF?usp=drive_link
In this example, we might need annotations for subsequences of the video
with 4s to 60s length with language instruction, start-time, end-time, a
quality score, and a speed score.

Here are some rough labelling guidelines for the scores we came up with:
Instruction:
Your task is to give the robot a score for each task execution. The score
will be between 0 (worst) and 10 (best). You are only going to judge the
end result; i.e. how happy a user would be with execution. Speed of
execution is not part of it unless it's specifically mentioned in the task
instruction.
0: injured or killed a human (>$1M cost)
1: endangered a human (> $10k cost)
2: destroyed a valuable object (>$100 cost)
3: costly error (destroyed an object, dropped an object that is not safe to
drop (plate, glass, ...))
4: negative task progress (e.g. moved away from target object)
5: not better or worse off
6: made some progress or shitty result
7: close to success or low quality result
8: most people would call it done
9: 80% (tiny imperfections)
10: 100% would call this successful (no human would see any error)

if score > 5, please provide a score for speed:
1: surprised it ever finished the task
5: average human speed
10: didn't know it could be done so fast

We will probably pre-label instructions with start and end-time in the
future. I assume we could provide a json for each video file with the
instruction, start, and end times. Would be great if you demonstrate how we
could do this tomorrow as well. I don't have an example for this file yet.

I think Nick also mentioned a "menu" of different labeller skill levels
with pricing. Would be great if you could share that with me before our
call tomorrow.

Best,
Alex

subject: Re: Encord & Kinisi Robotics
text:
Hi all,

Since we weren't able to cover the key questions we shared last time, I'll
paste a diagram that closely reflects our workflow (data preparation, minus
training), and the one we'd like to discuss:

[image: image.png]

The key questions we're looking to answer when evaluating data platforms
are related to this workflow:

   -

   How will your platform speed up and scale our model training workflow?
   -

      What parts of the pipeline (see NVIDIA pipeline
      <https://github.com/NVIDIA-Omniverse-blueprints/synthetic-manipulation-motion-generation?tab=readme-ov-file>)
      does it facilitate, implement, solve for us?
      - We'd like to focus on dataset curation, dataset augmentation, and
      training job integration
      - We have a 'desired features' list we'd like to go through
   -

   What would our data pipeline look like using your product?
   -

      Could we create a diagram together ? What is different, what parts
      run on your infrastructure? → how does it tie into our own infrastructure
      running on AWS (training jobs)?
      -

      How does your platform tie into our MLOps, and data preparation /
      curation / augmentation pipeline (which looks like the diagram above)?

Looking forward to the meeting!

Lucas
